Meeting header:

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Samira: Okay hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Samira from Redwood, and with me is Noah our SE. Hi Noah.
[00:00:05] Noah: Hey, hi all.
[00:00:07] Ellen: Hi, thanks. Sorry for the handful of us joining, we had a calendar overlap.
[00:00:12] Samira: No worries, great to meet you Ellen, Carlos, Priya, Jamal. Quick agenda: console walkthrough focused on per-route economics, how to read the charts, and then a short chat about pilots and SOX/SOC2 compliance. Sound good?
[00:00:25] Priya: Yes, mostly FinOps here so we want to understand cost drivers.
[00:00:29] Carlos: We're more interested in how easy it is to map routes from our gateway to console routes.
[00:00:33] Noah: Perfect. I'll share my screen and jump into the console. Quick note: audio might auto-cap-- if anything is garbled shout out.
[00:00:45] [screen share starts] Noah: Alright, here's the landing page, usage lenses. You can see token volume over time, request QPS, and a per-route list to the right.
[00:00:55] Ellen: Hmm the per-route view, will that pick up our internal endpoint names or do we have to define mapping?
[00:01:03] Noah: Good question. We support automatic route inference for common gateways, but for reliability I recommend defining an explicit mapping file. You can upload a mapping or use our SDK to annotate requests with route metadata.
[00:01:18] Carlos: That would be ideal. We run Kong in front of the model endpoints. Does the mapping need to be in headers?
[00:01:24] Noah: Headers or a small JSON payload, either works. We have examples for Kong, Envoy, and custom proxies in the docs. I'll drop the Kong snippet after the call.
[00:01:36] [00:01:36] Ellen: Great.
[00:01:38] Noah: Ok per-route dashboard: top-left is tokens and cost per route. Notice the split: compute cost vs storage/caching, and then a token breakdown that attributes prompt vs completion tokens and model variant.
[00:01:53] Priya: How accurate is the per-route cost? We need it to reconcile monthly invoices.
[00:01:59] Samira: It's based on per-token accounting plus per-inference overheads we measure in the runtime. For reconciliation we provide a CSV export with the same math we use for billing. Many customers plug that into their ledger.
[00:02:11] Priya: CSV export, good. Does it show per-token price applied?
[00:02:14] Samira: Yep, per-token unit price and the model/variant used.
[00:02:18] [00:02:18] Jamal: On latency, we care p50 and p99 for a couple of routes. Does the console show those metrics per route?
[00:02:25] Noah: Yes, p50/p90/p99 and CPU/GPU utilization for the serving pools. We also surface miss rates for the KV cache and batching efficiency.
[00:02:36] Ellen: You said KV cache miss rates—when would we expect miss rates to affect p99?
[00:02:41] Noah: If you rely on prefix caching for chat-style interactions, a high miss rate forces more compute per request, so p99 climbs. There's a tradeoff knob where you can prefer lower cost (higher batching, more quantized models) or lower latency (dedicated pools, higher batch priority).
[00:02:55] Carlos: Can you give a concrete example for our helpdesk route? Right now it's synched at 3 tokens per message (typo, meant 300 tokens) average and 25 QPS.
[00:03:05] Noah: Sure: take 25 QPS with 300 tokens average. On a hosted gpt-like model variant that's say X tokens per cent cost... (transcription note: model names sometimes garbled). If you enable KV caching for session history, we can cache the recent 5 messages and reduce tokens by roughly 40% depending on prompt template. That reduces per-route spend but may add ~20ms to some request paths on cache lookup, depending on your topology.
[00:03:30] Priya: That 40% sounds optimistic — how stable is that?
[00:03:33] Noah: It depends on conversation style. For ticket summarization it's very stable. For open-ended chat it's lower. We typically recommend running a 1-2 week pilot to measure actual delta.
[00:03:46] Priya: Okay makes sense.
[00:03:48] [00:03:48] Samira: On dedicated vs hosted — a lot of customers start hosted and then move to a dedicated pool for high-throughput routes. Dedicated gives you more control over quantization profiles and kernel selection, which reduces cost per token but requires commit.
[00:04:02] Priya: Commit as in reserved capacity contracts?
[00:04:05] Samira: Exactly, monthly or annual reserved capacity. We can show committed vs burst capacity pricing side-by-side.
[00:04:12] Ellen: We have strict latency SLOs for our primary support route — p99 < 300ms. Is that realistic on hosted or do we need dedicated?
[00:04:22] Noah: Depends on model size and sequence length. For short prompts and medium models, hosted with smart routing to low-latency pools can hit that, but it's more consistent on dedicated with pinned kernels. We'll include sample SLO profiles in the benchmark runbook.
[00:04:36] Carlos: Any region constraints? We are EU-first for some customers.
[00:04:40] Samira: We have regions in EU and NA. For private deployments we support V P C peering and on-prem if needed.
[00:04:48] Jamal: Does Redwood support customer-managed KMS? We cannot have keys in a shared KMS.
[00:04:53] Samira: Yes, we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for Private deployments; hosted customers can bring their own KMS in some tiers. We'll send our security integration doc.
[00:05:03] Ellen: Can you show the cost drilldown for a sample route?
[00:05:07] Noah: Sure — picking the helpdesk route: here's tokens over time, here's cost bar with model selection, batching efficiency, and percent saved by caching. See this spike on Jan 4th? That's an unusual batch due to a bot test. We can annotate events manually.
[00:05:25] Priya: Is the cost per-token shown in USD only or do you support multi-currency?
[00:05:30] Noah: Currently USD, but export can be converted client-side; multi-currency display is on the roadmap.
[00:05:36] Carlos: What about function-calling / tools costs? We call external tools a lot, any extra charges?
[00:05:42] Samira: We show external tool invocation counts but don't bill those; billing is per-token and per-inference overhead. Tool invocation cost is something we annotate for observability but not a billing line item currently.
[00:05:54] Ellen: Ok good to know.
[00:05:56] [00:05:56] Noah: Now switching to the Optimize tab — this suggests batching and quantization profiles based on observed latency windows and token length distributions. For your helpdesk route with long-ish completions, it flags that using 4-bit quantization on that model could reduce cost ~25% with minimal quality regression.
[00:06:16] Priya: How do you measure quality regressions? We need objective checks.
[00:06:19] Noah: We run eval sets and A/B compare outputs and present a small quality delta metric. You can plug in your own eval prompts and set alert thresholds.
[00:06:29] Ellen: Can you fall back automatically if quality drops below threshold?
[00:06:32] Noah: Yes, there are automatic fallback policies — canary to higher precision model or reroute to dedicated capacity.
[00:06:38] Carlos: One more question about the per-route mapping: does mapping tie into RBAC so different teams only see their routes?
[00:06:44] Samira: We have role-based access. You can restrict routes by team or project. We also support SAML/SSO. (transcription: SAML sometimes logged as SAM L).
[00:06:55] [00:06:55] Priya: For procurement, we'll need SOC2 and ISO docs and a sample contract.
[00:07:02] Samira: We'll attach SOC2 Type II and ISO certs. For contracts we have standard MSA + SLAs for Dedicated and Private.
[00:07:11] Jamal: About the CSV reconciliation — does it include request IDs to cross-ref with our logs?
[00:07:16] Noah: Yes, exports can include request_id, route, tokens, model, and cost line. That makes ledger reconciliation straightforward.
[00:07:25] Ellen: Great.
[00:07:27] [00:07:27] Samira: Quick pause — any blockers you're worried about? Priya?
[00:07:31] Priya: Top concerns are predictable monthly spend, and compliance. We need to see how unit economics map to our finance forecasts.
[00:07:38] Samira: Understood — we'll supply a sample forecast model with sensitivity (QPS, tokens, caching gains).
[00:07:45] Carlos: For the pilot, do we need to commit to any capacity?
[00:07:48] Samira: No, pilots run on hosted. If you want predictable p99, we can provision a short-term dedicated pool for the pilot at discounted commit.
[00:07:58] Priya: Discounted commit sounds like a negotiation point for our finance.
[00:08:03] Samira: Totally. We'll include a pilot pricing option.
[00:08:07] [00:08:07] Noah: Wrapping up the console tour — bookmarks, alerts, and a route heatmap that shows where cost is concentrated by customer cohort. You can open a route and see top prompt templates driving tokens.
[00:08:20] Ellen: That prompt template view is huge for us. We already have a couple templates that are expensive, seeing that will help triage.
[00:08:26] Samira: Good. We'll make sure Noah shares a short guide on how to create prompt sets for quality monitoring.
[00:08:33] Carlos: Any reference customers using this for billing chargeback?
[00:08:37] Samira: A few — I'll share anonymized case studies, especially customers who set up route-level chargeback.
[00:08:44] [00:08:44] Priya: Timeline wise — our procurement cycle is tight; ideally a contract in 6 weeks.
[00:08:50] Samira: Noted. We'll try to align pilot and procurement to that timeline.
[00:08:55] Jamal: Minor note — is there an API to pull per-route metrics so we can feed into our internal dashboards?
[00:09:01] Noah: Yes, there's an insights API. It returns the same metrics as the console; we'll include rate limits in the runbook.
[00:09:09] Ellen: Awesome.
[00:09:11] [screen share ends]
[00:09:15] Samira: Quick recap of what we said and next steps: 1) Samira sends pricing matrix + SOC2/ISO links, 2) Noah sends benchmark runbook and Kong mapping snippet, 3) Ellen to send route mapping and SLOs, 4) we schedule pilot kickoff week of Jan 19. Anything else?
[00:09:37] Priya: Please include an example reconciliation CSV.
[00:09:40] Samira: Will do.
[00:09:42] Carlos: Also include a note about the KV cache tradeoffs and the percent savings estimate you quoted.
[00:09:47] Noah: I'll add conservative and optimistic estimates in the runbook.
[00:09:51] Ellen: Thanks everyone.
[00:09:53] Samira: Thanks, we'll send follow-ups.
[00:09:56] [call ends]
